title: Roof Garden rivals: Faith Marable's band and Harvey Lightfoot
summary: The Roof Garden hired two bands; Williams recalls Faith Marable's visiting riverboat band and its players, then a break when company arrives.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Then we had, uh, Dandy Lewis on bass. You heard of him. Yeah, I've heard Bess talk about him. That's right. Dandy Lewis. That's who we had on bass. Then after Buddy Johnson left, we taken Earl Umphrey on trombone. He played up there with us. Then... Manny Mineta come up there with us a while. Yeah, he told us he did. Yeah, he come up. He played with us a while. We had a nice band. Five band. We used to have two bands. Celestine, our band, and they had the big carnival bars. They hired two bands. Sometime they'd hire Faith Marable. He had his band up there. He had his whole band up there. Oh, yeah. Come off the boat. Come up there and play late. You know what I see? Oh, yeah. He had a fine band. 25, from 25 to 27. Fine band. Who was with Faith about that time? Around by that time, he had Dewey Jackson. You remember Dewey? Well, I never met him. Fine trumpet, yeah. Fine trumpet playing. We had, uh, had this boy on trombone. Little Light Boy out of St. Louis. He had a band of his own after that. Harvey Lightfoot. Harvey Lightfoot.
Something like that? Or was it Lawson?

No, Harvey Lightfoot. Harvey Lightfoot. Yeah, that's his name. He's on record, too. Yeah. Harvey, wait. Is he still living? I don't know. Harvey Lightfoot. Mm-hmm. And he had a drummer. What's his drummer name? He live in Chicago. Now, a singing drummer. He sings well. Camel. Oh, yes. Camel. Floyd. That's right. Floyd Camel. That's right. He on piano. And, uh, what's this trombone player name? Natty Dominic? Nat, Nat, Nat, Nat. Nat, Nat. A trombone. Fine trombone. That's him. That's right. That story. St. Louis. That's right. That story. That's him. Fine trombone player. Yeah, let me see now. Who else on? Well, sometime he had old man Kimball on bass. Kimball's father. Yeah. Yeah, he and him. He worked for him a long time. I believe he was on bass then. I've waited for him a long time. And he had another little guy on banjo. He told me he went to penitentiary. He killed a man in New York. A little light fella. I can't think of his name. He must have went penitentiary. My older. Early thirties. Yeah. Fine banjo player. A little light boy. If I had to call his name, you might know him. Fine. Gets fine. Open the door. Looks like we have company.
I think before Andy came in, you were telling about when you played up the roof garden and Fates band.
Did they have two bands that were lights? Two bands. Two bands. Yeah. They had a better band. A fine band.
It was always a big band, but I bet your band played just as exciting as they did. I guess we imagined it. Yeah, sure. Just because they were bigger, it was better.
We thought they were bigger. But they were fine. Yeah.
